challenges.headline: One contract, one invoice assumed
challenges.premise: The request implies a signed contract produces a single invoice at signature.
challenges.alternative: In this platform a contract is explicitly one-to-many with its invoices — milestones, recurring billing and partial amounts are normal. The real deliverable may be a billing schedule generator, not a single document.
challenges.consequence: Building a single auto-created invoice when the client actually needs a billing schedule means the whole data model and workflow get rebuilt once the gap surfaces, likely after go-live.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with the client whether any contract type bills in installments or recurrence before estimating or building anything.

challenges.headline: Signature as synchronous trigger
challenges.premise: Invoice creation is implicitly expected to happen immediately and inline at the moment of signature.
challenges.alternative: An asynchronous, queued trigger with a visible pending state tolerates incomplete contract data and lets the invoice land as a reviewable draft rather than failing in the user's face during signature.
challenges.consequence: A synchronous design forces an answer, mid-signature, to what happens when billing data (amount, VAT rate, billing contact) isn't ready — a case this platform's own traps call out explicitly.
challenges.recommendation: Decide explicitly: synchronous-blocking vs. queued-eventual, and draft vs. issued as the invoice's initial state.

challenges.headline: One rule for every client
challenges.premise: The request treats auto-invoicing as a single global rule to implement once.
challenges.alternative: This platform's own configurability model expects billing logic, approval requirements and even whether auto-invoicing applies at all to vary by client or contract type.
challenges.consequence: Hardcoding a uniform rule now means the first client exception (no auto-invoice, or an approval step first) forces a redesign rather than a configuration change.
challenges.recommendation: Settle whether this is global behavior or configurable per client/contract type before locking the implementation shape.

challenges.headline: One invoice per signed contract
challenges.premise: The request implicitly treats 'invoice the contract' as creating a single invoice record when the contract is signed.
challenges.alternative: Driving creation from the contract's billing structure (one-off, milestone, recurring, partial) produces the correct number of invoices over time instead of one that may not match the deal.
challenges.consequence: Building for a single invoice first means re-architecting the moment a milestone or subscription contract appears — a near-certainty given the platform already models one-to-many contract-to-invoice billing.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm the billing structure(s) this automation must cover before writing the trigger.

challenges.headline: Sync vs async creation trigger
challenges.premise: The request treats invoice creation as something that simply 'happens' on signature, without specifying whether it blocks the signature action.
challenges.alternative: An async, queued creation with a visible pending state tolerates incomplete contract data and retries without putting the signature flow at risk.
challenges.consequence: A synchronous, blocking build means a failed invoice creation (missing field, bad amount source) can fail the signature itself in front of the client.
challenges.recommendation: Decide sync-vs-async explicitly with engineering before estimating, and design duplicate-prevention for re-signature/amendments at the same time.

challenges.headline: Auto-issue vs draft review
challenges.premise: The request assumes the auto-created invoice can go out without a human checkpoint.
challenges.alternative: Creating the invoice as a draft for finance/admin review before issuance keeps a human in the loop for the first release, catching amount or VAT errors before they reach a client.
challenges.consequence: Immediate issuance on an automated, unreviewed path multiplies the blast radius of any data or billing-rule mistake — each one is now a client-facing legal document.
challenges.recommendation: Settle who can see/approve the invoice before go-live, and whether that differs from today's manual process.

challenges.headline: Auto-created means auto-sent

challenges.headline: Signature event fires once
challenges.premise: The contract-signed event is treated as a single, clean trigger.
challenges.alternative: Design the trigger as idempotent from day one (a dedup key per contract+event), since retries and duplicate event delivery are normal in event-driven systems.
challenges.consequence: Without idempotency, a retried or duplicated event silently creates a second invoice — the kind of error that's discovered by the client, not by QA.
challenges.recommendation: Make idempotent invoice creation a non-negotiable part of the first build, not a later hardening pass.
